s: wunderkind, child prodigy (highly talented person who rises to excellence in their field at a young age)
Capa­blanca galt als Wunderkind, schon als Fünfjähriger soll er gegen erfahrene Spieler gewonnen haben, als Zwölfjähriger schlug er dann den Landesmeister im Schach.
Amfortas! Die Wunde! Die Wunde! Sie brennt mir hier zur Seite! O, Klage! Klage! Furchtbare Klage!
Amfortas! The wound! The wound! It burns me here to the side! O, complaint! Complaint! Terrible complaint!
Und sitzt die Wunde tief in deinem Inneren / Kannst du dich nicht erinnern?
Wunde.et: From Middle High German wunde, from Old High German wunta, from Proto-Germanic *wundō (“a wound”), from *wundaz (“wounded”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wen-. Compare Low German Wunn, Dutch wond, English wound, Icelandic und.

wund.et: From Middle High German wunt, from Old High German wunt, from Proto-West Germanic *wund, from Proto-Germanic *wundaz (“wounded”), from the verb *wundōną.

Wunder.et: From Middle High German wunder, wunter, from Old High German wuntar, from Proto-Germanic *wundrą, from Proto-Indo-European *wenh₁- (“to wish for, desire, strive for, win, love”). Compare German Low German Wunder, Wunner, Dutch wonder, English wonder, Danish un…

Wunsch.et: From Middle High German wunsch, from Old High German wunsc, from Proto-Germanic *wunskō, from Proto-Indo-European *wenh₁- (“to wish, love”). Compare Dutch wens, English wish, West Frisian winsk, Danish ønske.

s: Der ganze Plan beruhte auf reinem Wunschdenken.
The whole plan was based purely on wishful thinking.
Wunschdenken.et: From Wunsch (“wish”) + Denken (“thinking”). Like English wishful thinking it seems to stem from the early 20th century, it being as yet unestablished which of the two is earlier.

s: to surprise, to astonish (of sights, behaviors, outcomes)
Meine Mutter hat sich ganz schön gewundert, als wir schon nach einer Viertelstunde zurück waren.
My mother was quite surprised when we were back already 15 minutes later.
to wonder, to consider something strange, to be confused
Sie wundern sich über den Inhalt des Kästchens.
They are confused by the contents of the casket.

wundern.et: From Middle High German wundern, from Old High German wuntarōn, from Proto-Germanic *wundrōną, derived from *wundrą (“miracle”) (German Wunder).

wunderbar.et: From Middle High German wunderbære (also wunderberen, wunderberende), equivalent to Wunder + -bar. Akin to German Low German wunnerbaar, Low German wunnerbor, Dutch wonderbaar, Saterland Frisian wunderboar, and also calques Danish, Norwegian Bokmål and Swedish…

s: Auf eine Klippe vorwärts tretend, sahen sie das alte, schwarze, wunderliche Holzgebäude im Grunde vor sich, von steilen Felsen sowie von hohen Bäumen umschattet.
wunderlich.et: From Middle High German wunderlich, wonderlich, from Old High German wuntarlīh, from Proto-West Germanic *wundralīk, from Proto-Germanic *wundralīkaz, equivalent to Wunder + -lich. Cognate with English wonderly.

s: 1912, Martin Luther, Lutherbibel von 1912, Psalm 105:5 (with KJV translation)
Remember his marvellous works that he hath done; his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth
„Du nimmst mich Wunder ! und so gelassen erträgst du einen solchen Verlust ?”
„You surprise me! and you take such a loss this calmly?”
Es nimmt mich wunder, wieso sie sich nicht bei mir meldet.
I'm curious why she doesn't reach out to me.
A hand-held firework emitting sparks, a sparkler.

a Nazi propaganda term from the final phase of World War Two referring to secret weapon designs claimed to be revolutionary and capable of winning the war for Germany (many of these were fictional and intended merely to strengthen morale, others were ineffective or not finalized)
magic bullet, panacea (a universal solution which solves all problems related to a particular issue)
Tatsächlich gab es 2021 in den USA einen Hype um Ivermectin. Eine Gruppe von Ärzten pries das Medikament als Wunderwaffe gegen Corona, es wirke auch präventiv.
In fact, there was hype about Ivermectin in the USA in 2021. A group of doctors praised the drug as a magic bullet against Corona, saying it also had a preventive effect.
Wunstorf (a town in Lower Saxony, Germany)
Wenn ihr dann wieder einsam seid / Das ist der wunde Punkt / Wissen wir, dass wir traurig waren / Aber nicht mehr den Grund
Und Liebesweisen tönen, / Wie du sie nie gehört, / Bis wundersüßes Sehnen / Dich wundersüß betört!
Die Frauen deiner Familie haben sich, so kommt es dir vor, nicht bewusst für oder gegen Kinder entschieden. Absolutes Wunschkind seist du gewesen, sagt dir deine Mutter.
It seems to you that the women in your family did not consciously decide for or against having children. You were absolutely a planned child, your mother tells you.
a town in the Upper Franconia region, Bavaria
a rural district of the Upper Franconia region, Bavaria; official name: Wunsiedel im Fichtelgebirge

to endure something while sitting (e.g., an overlong play or film); to wait a long time for something while sitting
